sentence: ___ — you'll get there early and find the best seats.
correct: The early bird catches the worm
explanation: <The early bird catches the worm> significa que quien madruga tiene ventaja.
tip: Idiom: quien madruga, tiene ventaja (6 words)

sentence: By recycling old furniture, we ___: we save money and help the planet.
correct: kill two birds with one stone
explanation: <Kill two birds with one stone> significa lograr dos cosas con una sola acción.
tip: Idiom with <birds>: lograr dos cosas a la vez (6 words)

sentence: Don't just promise to help — ___.
explanation: <Actions speak louder than words> significa que lo que haces importa más que lo que dices.
tip: Idiom: lo que haces importa más que lo que dices (5 words)

sentence: Before the meeting starts, let's make sure we're ___.
explanation: <On the same page> significa estar de acuerdo o compartir el mismo entendimiento.
tip: Idiom with <page>: estar de acuerdo (4 words)

sentence: She always ___ for her students, staying late to help them.
explanation: <Go the extra mile> significa hacer un esfuerzo especial.
tip: Idiom with <mile>: hacer un esfuerzo extra (4 words)

sentence: I lost my wallet, but I found a better one — ___.
correct: every cloud has a silver lining
explanation: <Every cloud has a silver lining> significa que hay algo bueno en cada situación mala.
tip: Idiom with <lining>: hay algo bueno en lo malo (6 words)

sentence: Apply for the scholarship now, or you'll ___.
explanation: <Miss the boat> significa perder una oportunidad.
tip: Idiom with <boat>: perder una oportunidad (3 words)

sentence: Keep practicing the piano — ___.
explanation: <Practice makes perfect> significa que la práctica constante mejora una habilidad.
tip: Idiom: la práctica mejora una habilidad (3 words)

sentence: These problems are just ___ — there's much more to fix.
explanation: <The tip of the iceberg> significa solo una pequeña parte de un problema mayor.
tip: Idiom with <iceberg>: solo una pequeña parte (5 words)

sentence: The small café looked boring, but the food was amazing — ___.
correct: don't judge a book by its cover
explanation: <Don't judge a book by its cover> significa no juzgar por las apariencias.
tip: Idiom with <book>: no juzgar por apariencias (7 words)

sentence: She ___ to finish her essay before the deadline.
explanation: <Burn the midnight oil> significa trabajar o estudiar hasta muy tarde.
tip: Idiom with <midnight>: trabajar hasta muy tarde (4 words, pasado)

sentence: Losing my job was ___ — I found a much better one.
explanation: <A blessing in disguise> significa algo malo que resulta ser bueno.
tip: Idiom with <blessing>: algo malo que resulta bueno (4 words)

sentence: My sister and I don't always ___ about politics.
explanation: <See eye to eye> significa estar de acuerdo con alguien.
tip: Idiom with <eye>: estar de acuerdo (4 words)

sentence: He'll clean his room ___.
explanation: <When pigs fly> significa que algo nunca va a suceder.
tip: Idiom with <pigs>: nunca va a pasar (3 words)

sentence: I'm just ___ — it was a joke!
explanation: <Pull someone's leg> significa tomarle el pelo a alguien.
tip: Idiom with <leg>: tomarle el pelo a alguien (3 words, gerundio)

sentence: Working from home gives me ___: freedom and comfort.
explanation: <The best of both worlds> significa disfrutar las ventajas de dos situaciones diferentes.
tip: Idiom with <worlds>: las ventajas de dos cosas (5 words)

sentence: His angry comments only ___.
explanation: <Add fuel to the fire> significa empeorar una situación.
tip: Idiom with <fuel>: empeorar una situación (5 words, pasado)

sentence: Taking five classes at once was ___.
correct: biting off more than I could chew
explanation: <Bite off more than you can chew> significa intentar hacer más de lo que puedes manejar.
tip: Idiom with <chew>: intentar hacer más de lo que puedes (7 words)

sentence: ___ this weekend — you deserve a rest.
explanation: <Take it easy> significa relajarse y no preocuparse.
tip: Idiom with <easy>: relajarse (3 words)

sentence: ___, I've actually met her before.
explanation: <As a matter of fact> significa de hecho, en realidad.
tip: Idiom: de hecho, en realidad (5 words)
